summary: Interactive class session hosted by Prof. Sharma (SPK-01) with active participation from Rahul Verma (SPK-02), Ananya Patel (SPK-03), and David Chen (SPK-04). The instructor demonstrated formatting in Jupyter Notebook Markdown cells, contrasting ordered lists (numeric) with unordered lists (symbols: filled circle, square, open circle). He explained hyperlink syntax [text](url) and image embedding ![alt](url) with alt text fallback. The session concluded with practical student questions on multimedia support and a homework assignment deadline.
keyPoints: [00:00] Prof. Sharma opens the session on Markdown formatting in Jupyter Notebooks.
[00:12] Ordered lists use sequential numbers, whereas unordered lists use tiered geometric bullets.
[00:36] Sub-point indentation dynamically alters bullets from filled circles to squares and empty circles.
[01:05] Hyperlink notation: bracketed label [Link text] followed immediately by URL in parentheses (url).
[01:54] Image notation: prefixed with an exclamation mark ![alt text](image url); displays fallback alt text if link fails.
[02:39] Multimedia (audio/video) can also be incorporated into notebook Markdown cells.
[03:02] Prof. Sharma assigns homework: create a formatted Markdown practice document due Friday at 5 PM.
insights: Multi-level indentation in Markdown cells creates intuitive semantic hierarchy for technical notes.
Descriptive alt text in image Markdown prevents broken-link ambiguity and enhances document accessibility.
Using Markdown cells for documentation directly alongside Python code cells improves reproducibility in Jupyter Notebooks.
